summary: Let the score of a nonnegative integer x be how many zeros sit at the end of x factorial written in base ten, and treat the factorial of zero as one. Read an integer K from the closed interval that runs from 0 through 10^9. Count how many nonnegative integers x have a score exactly equal to K, and write that count.
